relations.subject: indexes:early-filtering
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - mustUseInsteadWhen predicate from watchlist/promoted relations; the documented condition is that a filter which cannot be reduced to an exact index span cannot use ordinary predicate pushdown and early filtering must be used instead
relations.evidence: In this case, the filter cannot be pushed down to the Index service. This is where early filtering comes into play. The Query service can apply the specified filter to the results of the index scan, before fetching the matching documents from the Data service.

relations.subject: indexes:early-order-and-pagination
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - mustUseInsteadWhen predicate; documents the condition (ORDER BY terms not aligned with index key order, or reverse-scan direction) under which order/pagination pushdown is unavailable and early ordering must be used instead
relations.evidence: However, if we change the order of the ordering terms so that they no longer match the index key order, ordering cannot be pushed down to the Index service. ... So in this case, early ordering, limit, and offset are done by the Query service before fetch.

relations.subject: indexes:early-filtering
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused, not minted - structural markdown link
relations.evidence: Index [pushdowns](index%5Fpushdowns.md) provide one way to reduce the amount of data to be fetched.

notable_absence.finding: The Limitations section lists precise structural conditions for early ordering/pagination to apply (single keyspace, no JOIN, no GROUP BY/aggregates, no IntersectScan/UnionScan/DistinctScan, parallelism disabled when active) but these are procedural constraints rather than candidate ontology relations - flagged here rather than force-fit into a relation.

cross_product_finding: This page mirrors server/current/indexes/early-filters-and-pagination.md and the server/7.2/7.6 equivalents almost verbatim, including identical example indexes (idx_eat_city_name, idx_landmark_city_name) and EXPLAIN output.
